description: Ex-RAAF Sioux painted to represent a US Army example. On display at the museum, formerly the Naval Aviation Museum and Australia Museum of Flight.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Iroquois delivered May 1964, coded 857/897 and later 882, in search and rescue configuration; a training aid at HMAS Nirimba before joining the museum.
Ex-US Army UH-1H recovered from the AMARC boneyard, donated by the US Army and airlifted to Nowra in 2004 by RAAF 36 Squadron; represents the RAN Helicopter Flight Vietnam.
The last Sycamore in Royal Australian Navy service, flown to HMAS Nirimba for apprentice training in July 1965 and on static display as 850 since August 1977.
Ex-Royal Australian Navy Sycamore coded 907, damaged in a 1956 incident and with a short service life.
Wirraway III in the museum collection.
Royal Australian Navy Macchi coded 868, re-serialled A7-077 on transfer to the RAAF in 1983.
aliases: MB326; MB326H; CA-30; CA30; Macchi; A7-077

description: Ex-Royal Australian Navy Sea Venom coded 878/M; RAN serial N4-935.
RAN serial N4-937, coded Y-211. Fitted with a replacement engine by 724 Squadron and regularly ground-run before going on permanent display.

Delivered to the Royal Australian Navy in 1957 and due to be transported to Canberra in 1972 but never left Nowra. Has been displayed wearing its own serial, that of XA101, and is currently marked XG766.
Royal Australian Navy Skyhawk. The airframe displayed as 882 is ex-US Navy A-4B BuNo 142874, repainted as 882 in 2007; a 2017 visit report attributes the display to N13-154903 instead.
Delivered 1971, sold to the RNZAF in 1982 and returned to Australia by RAAF C-17A on 23 April 2012; repainted in RAN 724 Squadron colours and returned to TA-4G appearance. Coded 880.
Royal Australian Navy Dakota delivered 1 February 1949, fitted out at one stage as a flying classroom with a Sea Venom radar nose to train Sea Venom and Gannet observers. Coded NW-800.
Royal Australian Navy Firefly used as a Nowra gate guard from 1965 to 1972, restored by volunteers from 1973 and displayed as 207/K, later 238/K.
Flew with 725, 816 and 817 Squadrons RAN; withdrawn 15 August 1967 and displayed as 846/M.
Returned to the Royal Navy and converted to T.5, then returned to the museum. Formerly displayed in Royal Navy markings, since restored to RAN scheme.
Front fuselage only. Ex-USAF FB-111A; part of this forward fuselage has been used to refurbish the cockpit of RAAF A8-132.

Stored dismantled at 6 Stores Depot Dubbo, then at Camden under Air Training Corps care, then at the rear of the museum from about 2008. Transported by road to the RAAF Amberley Aviation Heritage Centre in February 2018, so it is no longer held here.
Royal Australian Navy target drone, previously RAAF A92-605.
Previously RAAF A92-609, delivered October 1969, damaged after a malfunction in 1971 and returned to service. Displayed on its launch trolley; constructor plates show c/n FR6.

Forward fuselage only. Ex-US Navy BuNo 151646, dropped into Sydney Harbour while being unloaded and used as an instructional airframe; displayed marked 853, a code that properly belongs to N12-152837.
Ex-US Navy BuNo 153582, withdrawn 12 August 1984; on display coded 859.
Royal Australian Navy Tracker in the museum collection.
Ex-Republic of Singapore Air Force Hunter carrying the number 280.
Millicer-designed Airtourer light aircraft.
Ex-Australian Defence Force MRH-90 Taipan.
US Navy-built MH-60R Seahawk coded 70.
Delivered 1987 to 816 Squadron and named Christine; withdrawn from service 29 July 2016 and placed on display.
Royal Australian Navy Squirrel coded 862, modified with a cabin-door 7.62mm machine gun for Gulf operations from 1990. Retired 2015 and delivered to the museum in December 2017.
Ex-RAAF PC-9/A delivered by truck to the museum on 26 October 2019 in a red and white scheme with a 2FTS badge on the tail.
Full-scale non-flying replica of the Sopwith Pup marked N5182. Recorded without a serial: the original N5182 survives in the United Kingdom and this airframe wears its marks.
Supermarine Sea Otter amphibian.
Royal Australian Navy Dragonfly under long-term restoration.

Delivered 20 March 1963 as WS101 and later serialled N8-101; coded 841 and 891. Withdrawn 1977, restored to flying condition as 891/VH-NVY and damaged in an accident at Schofields. The registration VH-NVY is now carried by the HARS Auster.
Cockpit and remains only. Ditched in 1975 with the crew rescued and recovered on 13 November 1975; components used as training aids. Displayed coded 906.
Gulf operations veteran flown by 817 Squadron as Shark 07; took part in the final Sea King formation flight before retirement on 15 December 2011.

Made a precautionary landing on Durras Beach after a loose alternator, was repaired and flown back to Nowra. Withdrawn 31 December 1989 and on display at the museum. The Australian War Memorial Wessex is N7-216, not this aircraft.
Royal Australian Navy Kalkara target drone.
Reproduction of the Lawrence Hargrave 1894 box kite man-lifting apparatus.
Australian single-seat ultralight.
